newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean petrochemical firms vow partial strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean petrochemical firms vow partial strike.

text.p: Unionised workers at South Korea's three petrochemical companies with naphtha crackers have decided to go on a two-day partial strike from Tuesday in protest at a new labour law, representatives from the unions said on Friday.
However, they said no production loss was expected and factories at Honam Petrochemical Corp, LG Petrochemical Co and Hanwha Petrochemical Corp would remain in operation despite the partial strike.

Other petrochemical companies, including Daelim Industrial Co, Hyundai Petrochemical Co, Yukong Ltd, and Korea Petrochemical Industry Co were also considering joining the strike but have no concrete plans.
Samsung General Chemical Co, a unit of Samsung Group, would not be affected because it does not have a labour union.
"We'll follow the decision made by the Federation of Korean Trade Unions to go on strike on Tuesday and Wednesday," said a union representative at LG Petrochemical, an affiliate of the federation.
"All union members in maintenance sectors and some in operational sectors will join the walkout. But the rest will stay and keep the operation going," he said.

The Federation of Korean Trade Unions, South Korea's biggest union body which claims 1.2 million members, called electricity, port and railway workers to go on partial strike and all other unionists to join a full stoppage for two days starting next Tuesday.
All unions at naphtha cracking firms except for Hyundai are under the federation.
Unionised workers at Hyundai, an affiliate of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, postponed a partial strike which was planned for last Thursday.
The union would decide on late Friday when to hold the strike.

Strikes have crippled much of South Korean industry since the new labour law allowing lay-offs, flexible work hours and the replacement of striking workers was rammed through parliament on December 26.
